done.why: I had just killed the troll, walked out to the river and back, and was about to try the stairs up out of the Loud Room when it told me I'd used all 30 turns. I was only just getting somewhere.

about: It's Zork, or something wearing Zork's clothes: a white house with a mailbox, a trap door under the rug, a troll in the cellar, and then a maze of caves with a deafening room and a cold grey river at the bottom of some cliffs. The parts I saw were the same old opening; the river description was the one place it felt like someone had put new words in.

moments.note: Leaflet says WELCOME TO ZORK outright. So it isn't hiding what it is.
Trap door slams and someone bars it behind me. Classic, but it still works.
Troll knocks me to my knees and I'm stuck recovering while he swings. Felt like dice, not choices.
Took the troll's head off and the body vanished in black fog. Good payoff after six swings.
Round Room says passages in all directions but several caved in. Which ones? It didn't say and I didn't have turns to try them all.
Beach description never mentions a river, even though a river is right there if you ask.
The river line - going downstream as if it had heard something about the end of it - was the first sentence that felt written for me.
South along the cliffs is a dead end. Two turns wasted out of thirty.
Turn cap hit right as I was about to go up the stairs. Thirty turns is barely enough to get past the troll.

wished: Try the stairs up from the Loud Room and actually find the dam I kept hearing about in the rushing noise.
Pick up the platinum bar in the Loud Room, or at least get told why I couldn't.
Have the Round Room tell me which passages were caved in instead of making me guess.
More than 30 turns. The fight alone ate six of them.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: First moment the place felt hostile instead of just old.

lines.line: It's curtains for the troll as your sword removes his head.
lines.why: The fight finally ended and the game had a bit of swagger about it.

lines.line: The room is deafeningly loud with an undetermined rushing sound.
lines.why: This is what told me there was water and probably a dam somewhere I never reached.

lines.line: The Frigid River is wide and grey and very cold, and in a hurry, going downstream as if it had heard something about the end of it and wanted to see for itself.
lines.why: Only line that read like a person wrote it for this version. Made me want to follow the river.

fun.why: The troll fight and the trap door slamming were genuinely fun; the walk to a dead-end beach and the turn cap right after were not.

engagement.why: I wanted to find the dam after the Loud Room and the river, but I spent most of my turns on the standard opening and a fight I couldn't influence.

difficulty.why: Nothing I did was hard to figure out; the troll was a matter of swinging until the dice went my way. The only real obstacle was the turn budget.

interestingness.why: Mostly the Zork I half-expected. The river line and the unexplained rushing sound hinted at something changed, but I never got far enough to see it.

prose.why: Terse and functional most of the time, with a couple of lines that had real flavor, the troll's death and especially the river.
